outcome.answer:
You can remove company trademarks and corporate slogans from LLM-generated text (while trying to preserve general knowledge/capabilities) using inference-time “unbranding” methods that neutralize textual trade-dress markers like slogans and characteristic brand language, without requiring parameter updates. One approach is MUTE, which iteratively optimizes system instructions to eliminate brand leakage while preserving the model’s general capabilities and utility. [1]

Alternatively, you can frame the task as explainable text redaction: use an instruction-tuned LLM to apply user-defined redaction rules (in natural language) to identify and redact sensitive brand identifiers in unstructured text, with transparent justifications and rule triggers. This targets selective removal and auditability rather than explicitly “unbranding” style markers. [2]

These differ in focus: [1] is specifically about neutralizing textual brand identity/trade dress during generation, while [2] is a more general, policy/rule-driven redaction framework. [1,2]
